# Introduction 

The following document is the user guide of the REST API for TMF931 Open Gateway Onboarding and Ordering Operate API. The GSMA Open Gateway initiative aims to establish standardized Service APIs (under CAMARA standard) but also homogeneous mechanisms for the integration of Channel Partners, enabling seamless integration and interoperability across various platforms and telecommunications service providers.

This Operate API component suite covers the operations required between the Channel Partners and the Operators as described in the GSMA Playbook ([https://www.gsma.com/](https://www.gsma.com/solutions-and-impact/gsma-open-gateway/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/Channel-Partner-Onboarding-Guide-WA.101-v1.0.pdf) [solutions-and-impact/gsma-open-gateway/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/Channel-Partner-](https://www.gsma.com/solutions-and-impact/gsma-open-gateway/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/Channel-Partner-Onboarding-Guide-WA.101-v1.0.pdf) [Onboarding-Guide-WA.101-v1.0.pdf)](https://www.gsma.com/solutions-and-impact/gsma-open-gateway/wp-content/uploads/2024/02/Channel-Partner-Onboarding-Guide-WA.101-v1.0.pdf).

This Operate API component suite implements a subset of the proposed scenarios:

- ApplicationOwner Management (acceptance, onboarding, lifecycle management)
- Application Management (acceptance, onboarding, lifecycle management)
- Service API Order Management (ordering, retrieving orders)
- Product Management (retrieving products) In the user guide and OAS :
- Aggregator is modelled as a Channel Partner
- Developer or ASP is modelled as an ApplicationOwner A Technical Playbook is work in progress under GSMA in order to restrict the possibilities of implementation of TMF931 by Operators and Channel Partners, for improved interoperability. At the time of release of this API version, this document is not yet validated and published. Further evolution of this API specification might implement decisions approved in this Technical Playbook.

## Domain Context Specialization

This API is a composite DCS (Domain Context Specialization) of 4 TMF API for Open Gateway context.

- TMF622 Product Ordering Management v5.0
- TMF637 Product Inventory Management v5.0
- TMF669 Party Role Management v5.0
- TMF639 Resource Inventory v5.0 This DCS API doesn’t yet fully follow the TMF DCS guidelines. Future evolutions of this API may apply those guidelines.

The internal translation of TMF931 operations and resources should be as follows :

- TMF931 POST /ApplicationOwner corresponds to TMF669 POST /partyRole. This TMF931 operation contains the Party (engagedParty) by value that is a difference vs the TMF669 standard.

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

- TMF931 POST /Application corresponds to TMF639 POST /logicalResource. This TMF931 operation returns the resourceRole of the Application as consumer of API products.
- TMF931 POST /ApiProductOrder corresponds to TMF622 POST /productOrder. This TMF931 operation includes a productAction that contains the configurable characteristics (replaces the product attribute in TMF622). Each orderItem is done for one application and one offer, but it allows have several orderItem in the same productOrder. During the processing of the “POST /apiProductOrder” to order a set of API offers, there is creation of “apiProduct” instances in the product inventory.
- TMF931 GET /ApiProduct corresponds to TMF637 GET /product. There is one “apiProduct” instance for each API offer being ordered for a specific Application. 2 Applications can’t therefore consume the same “apiProduct” instance.

## Scenarios

The actors involved in this Open Gateway API can be seen in the figure:

![](data:image/jpeg;base64,)

- Operators are CSP (Communications Service Provider) that provide value to Channel Partner through the use of Operate APIs.
- The Channel Partner (CP) are providers/aggregators who offer its services to one or more ApplicationOwners.
- ApplicationOwners create Applications that are acquired and utilized by end users
- End users are the ApplicationOwner customers at the end of the value chain and are the ultimate beneficiaries of the value offered by the Operate APIs.

This Operate API focuses on the operations between Channel Partners and Operators. The operations allow to subscribe to Service APIs, manage subscriptions; create and manage ApplicationOwners; and create and manage Applications for ApplicationOwners.

The ordering (API subscription/unsubscription) is done on offers exposed to ApplicationOwners via the TMF936 Product Catalog API DCS for Open Gateway.

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

The GSMA Open Gateway initiative takes into account two different business models:

- In the Wholesale Reseller model, the service is fully managed by the Channel Partner.
- In the Aggregated Marketplace model, the Channel Partner leverages its Marketplace to individually expose the APIs. To ensure a coherent user experience, a UX layer is applied, creating a unified interface for the ApplicationOwner.

This Operate API considers the two models defined in GSMA Open Gateway and both can be implemented by using it.

## Catalog modelling (from TMF936 User Guide)

The examples in the OAS and User Guide are based on this ficticious catalog model.

Disclaimer: All prices examples appearing in this specification are fictitious. Any resemblance to real offers is purely coincidental.

Bundle offer (Operator internal view) :

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/jpeg;base64,)

The product catalog offers for Open Gateway Location Verification a flexible model based on subscription and usage volume for an API verification service. The main offering is the Open Gateway bundle offer, which allows users to add or remove components based on their specific needs. This structure provides an adaptable solution for different use cases.

Within this offering, there are two main location verification included offerings. The first one, Location Verification v1 CAMARA API Bundled, includes the Camera API as part of a package and is specifically marketed for fraud prevention and detection.

The second included offering, Location Verification Verify Usage Volume Recurring, follows a usage-based model with recurring cost, enabling continuous access to the service. Both included offerings can be configured dynamically based on user requirements.

Standalone offer (Operator internal view) :

![](data:image/png;base64,)

The concepts of ProductSpecification and ProductOffering permits Channel Partner to know which are the offerings made upon a same unique ProductSpecification.

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

An Operator can design as many atomic ProductOffering as he needs based on a same ProductSpecification. An atomic ProductOffering can be based on maxiumum 1 ProductSpecification. A composite ProductOffering (bundle, package, …) is composed of atomic ProductOfferings or composite ProductOfferings.

Important notice : it has been decided to simplifiy this view for the Channel Partner. We consider that the action (add, delete, modify) done at the atomic productOffering level applies same at its related productSpecification level. This implies that the product instantiated from an atomic productOffering order (action add) aggregates the instance of the atomic productOffering and the instance of the productSpecification. Inside the Operator IT it could be 2 separated products, but the view given to Channel Partner is only one product. For a composite productOffering, each productOffering that is part of the composition (including the main composite offer itself) has an instantiated product created for each productOffering that has an action add on the order. It also implies that the product order contains only the id of the productOfferings (not the id of the productSpecifications) but their productAction contain productSpecification characteristics, so apply to the ProductSpecification.

In the examples below, the id are the last 3 characters of the full id present in the OAS examples of TMF936 and TMF931. This aims to provide comprehensive understanding of the OAS examples based on these diagrams. Please note that the ProductOrder examples in OAS are not represented in these diagrams. In TMF931 there are :

- 1 example of order with action add for the standalone ProductOffering/ProductSpecification
- 1 example of order with action delete for the standalone Product (instance of the standalone ProductOffering/ProductSpecification)
- 1 example of order with 3 order items : 1 item with action add for the bundle ProductOffering/ProductSpecification, 1 item with action add for the atomic API ProductOffering/ProductSpecification and 1 item with action add for the atomic usage volume ProductOffering/ProductSpecification. These 3 order items are in relationship, keeping same relationships as in the diagram. The 3 order items are mandatory to fulfil the order. This permits to pass the necessary characteristics (in ProductAction) and other attributes that are specific for each ProductOffering/ProductSpecification.

## Limitations of this specification version

This version of this Operate API permits to implement the ordering and retrieval of products that are not only API products, so permits to manage bundle (composite product) and usage volume product. But to maintain backward compatibility it has been decided to keep the ApiProduct and ApiProductOrder schemas that fit for API products, but not so much for composite bundle product or for usage volume product. A further version of this API might propose a better fitted set of schemas for other kind of products that are not API.

| failed | Order item as not a successful deliverycompletion. The product is not delivered and theorder item failed. All Order items have failedwhich results in the entire Order has Failed. |
| partial | Some Order items have failed and some havesucceeded so the entire Order is in a Partialstate. This provides support for partial Failure ofan Order. This state is not available at item level |

- The choice to accept order is done for the complete order and we cannot have a partial acceptance with some item in rejected and some other in acknowledged.

## Error Management

In error handling different cases must be considered, even at the functional level that it is possible to modify the error message returned to the API consumer. For this error handling there are two possible alternatives listed below:

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

- Error handling done with custom policies in the API admin tool.
- Error management performed in a service queried by API.

The essential requirements to consider would be:

- Error handling should be centralized in a single place, regardless of whether they are APIs that are proxies to end services or APIs that invoke an integrator service on the ESB.
- Customization of the generated error based on the error content returned by the final core service should be contemplated.
- Latency should be minimized in its management.

In the following, we elaborate on the existing client errors. In particular, we identify the different error codes and cluster them into separate tables, depending on their nature: i) syntax exceptions, ii) service exceptions, and iii) server errors.

## Strongly typed schemas for characteristics

### Introduction

A Product Ordering business process requires the execution of a series of previous actions (including API calls) in a defined order so that the process can be carried out correctly. Like the more generic product ordering process managed with TMF Product Ordering, the specialized API Product Ordering is also catalog-oriented, so in order to be carried out it needs to know, through the execution of previous steps, the specifications of the products to be delivered in the order, as well as the actions required by the requester on these products. There is a clear alignment between the way a product is modelled in the product catalog and the way this product can be ordered via an API Product Order call. The modelling of the productSpecification or ProductOffering in the Product Catalog has also an impact on the way the Product is finally reflected in the product inventory.

With the ApiProductOrder resource definition as a specialization of a ProductOrder resource, a new way to ensure such alignment has been introduced: the use of strongly typed referenced schemas for ProductOrderItem and ProductAction. The underlying idea can be summarized as follows: each ProductSpecification managed in an ApiProductOrder requires a set of optional or mandatory attributes to be valued by the API client to ensure its successful delivery. The attributes to be in input depend on the productSpecification definition and the action to be performed over it (add, modify or delete), as each product may require different information. A schema-based model is mandatory : there are for each ProductSpecification definition a reference to N ProductAction schemas, one for each possible action available over that ProductSpecification (via a ProductOffering). Each schema includes the corresponding set of attributes necessary for that ProductOffering/ProductSpecification to be delivered via an ApiProductOrder. Same applies for the ApiProduct : for each ProductSpecification there is a reference to an ApiProduct schema that includes the corresponding set of attributes necessary for that ApiProduct description.

ProductAction replaces the product passed in the TMF622 orderItem. The idea is that productAction contains only productSpecification configured characteristic during the order

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

(purpose, …) + reference of the application. This permits to avoid to use the standard product attribute that contains the full Product schema that would not be useful because needed only for characteristics.

### Examples

Warning: these examples may not be 100% alinged with the OAS schemas, this is illustrative to understand the use of strongly typed schemas and the @schemaLocation to retrieve dynamically the schemas that permit to validate the payload.

Let’s take the example of a Device Location Verification API that is offerd through an atomic ProductOffering based on a ProductSpecification. Let’s assume that this ProductSpecification describes a specific characteristic for this API (coming from the Customer Facing Service definition) : bestAccuracy. This characteristic is not in the common schemas ApiProduct and ProductSpecification, so it’s not described in the OAS, because the OAS can’t contain all specific schemas from all product specifications that will be exposed in all Operator catalogs. This rule permits to not having to upgrade the Operate API OAS each time a new ProductSpecification is added into an Operator catalog.

We need to use specialized schemas that will allow this specific characteristic to be valued and read by the Operate API client. So it has to be described in a JSON schema that the API client can discover. The way TMF decided to do is :

- @type : name of the schema. It can be the standard name of schema from OAS, or can be a specific name because the schema needs to be specialized
- @schemaLocation : URL of the json schema describing the schema used in the payload. This attribute is not mandatory when @type value is the standard OAS schema; but becomes mandatory when the @type is the name of a schema not in the OAS.
- @baseType : can be used when the schema is specialized in order to indicate the parent schema

**ApiProductDeviceLocationVerification.schema.json**

This is the JSON schema that describes the specialized ApiProduct schema for Device Location Verification. The API client needs it when it will receive for API server a payload with an @type:ApiProductDeviceLocationVerification.

```
{
    "$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#",
    "$id": "ApiProductDeviceLocationVerification.schema.json",    "title": "ApiProductDeviceLocationVerification",
    "definitions": {
        "ApiProductDeviceLocationVerification": {
            "type": "object",            "properties": {
                "bestAccuracy": {
                    "type": "integer"
                }            },
            "allOf": [            {
                "$ref": "https://.../ApiProduct.schema.json#/definitions/ApiProduct"            }
```

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

  \]   }

  } }

## Monitor pattern

Monitor pattern is described in TMF630 REST guidelines.

# A classic interaction with Asynchronous response and monitor pattern looks like below:

# Channel Partner

# 1 TMF931 POST /ApplicationOwner (Reason, ProductOrder)

| HTTP Status: 202 AcceptedHTTP Header:Location: https://mycsp.com/tmf-api/openGatewayOperateAPIOnboardingAndOrdering/v5/applicationOwner/{applicationOwnerID}**2** Link: \< https://mycsp.com/tmf-api/openGatewayOperateAPIOnboardingAndOrdering/v5/applicationOwner/{applicationOwnerID}\>;rel="self",\< https://mycsp.com/tmf-api/openGatewayOperateAPIOnboardingAndOrdering/v5/monitor/{monitorID}\>;rel="related";title="monitor",  | **3** Processing the task |
| --- | --- |
| **4** TMF931 GET /monitor/{monitorID} | **3** Processing the task |
| **4** TMF931 GET /monitor/{monitorID} |  |
| **4** TMF931 GET /monitor/{monitorID} |  |
| **5** HTTP Status: 200 OK |  |

# Processing the task

# Channel Partner

# In the above example we can notice the following:

The client does not send any header to indicate to the server if it would like a synchronous answer or an asynchronous answer (no Expect Header used).

# According to the API definition, the server can return either 201 Created or 202 Accepted - meaning that it can support both patterns (synchronous and asynchronous) and is up for the server implementation to decide or if there is support for the client to decide via the Expect

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

header.

The server is:

- returning a 202 Accepted HTTP Status Code - representing the asynchronous behavior
- returning a Location header to indicate to the consumer the path to the applicationOwner resource. In this case, the server is able to provide as part of the response the applicationOwnerID.

The location path can look something like this:

Location: [https://mycsp.com/tmf-api/openGatewayOperateAPIOnboardingAndOrdering/v5/](https://mycsp.com/tmf-api/openGatewayOperateAPIOnboardingAndOrdering/v5/applicationOwner/e05b75dc-f843-40d9-8d16-112275a28385) [applicationOwner/e05b75dc-f843-40d9-8d16-112275a28385 ](https://mycsp.com/tmf-api/openGatewayOperateAPIOnboardingAndOrdering/v5/applicationOwner/e05b75dc-f843-40d9-8d16-112275a28385)(where 31 is the applicationOwner identifier)

Note If the server is unable to provide a resource identifier, then it must provide the monitor resource. The link to the actual resource (self)

- Link: [https://mycsp.com/tmf-api/openGatewayOperateAPIOnboardingAndOrdering/v5/](https://mycsp.com/tmf-api/openGatewayOperateAPIOnboardingAndOrdering/v5/applicationOwner/e05b75dc-f843-40d9-8d16-112275a28385) [applicationOwner/e05b75dc-f843-40d9-8d16-112275a28385;](https://mycsp.com/tmf-api/openGatewayOperateAPIOnboardingAndOrdering/v5/applicationOwner/e05b75dc-f843-40d9-8d16-112275a28385)rel=self,

Due to the fact that the server is implementing a "monitor" pattern it will also return the relevant "hypermedia links"

The link to the monitor resource, where the consumer can check regularly in order to check the status of the operation

- Link: [https://mycsp.com/tmf-api/openGatewayOperateAPIOnboardingAndOrdering/v5/](https://mycsp.com/tmf-api/openGatewayOperateAPIOnboardingAndOrdering/v5/monitor/987654) [monitor/987654;](https://mycsp.com/tmf-api/openGatewayOperateAPIOnboardingAndOrdering/v5/monitor/987654)rel=related;title=monitor, (where the 987654 is the monitor resource identifier assigned for this resource)

Note : This pattern can be done for PATCH operations also.

# Sample Use Cases 

This section explains how the functions are implemented using the Onboarding Operate API. As mentioned above, there are three groups of operations in this API:

- Application Service Provider (ApplicationOwner) Management This functional area covers the management of a ApplicationOwner as a Party Role. This includes the creation of the ApplicationOwner PartyRole in this context. It also covers the retrieval of the ApplicationOwner.

\*Application Management This functional area covers the management of the LogicalResource representing the Application in the Channel Partner Resource Inventory. This includes the creation of the Application as a LogicalResource + its LogicalResourceRole in this context. This Application, created in the Channel Partner resource inventory has to be known by the Operator. The Operator will then have to create this representation of this Application in a dedicated resource inventory.

An Application is modeled as a subclass of a LogicalResource.

It covers also the deletion of the Application from the Channel Partner side.

- Products Management This functional area covers the Channel Partner ordering the Operator for an API to be consumed by an Application. This requirement is mandatory as it’s the core need for this API business requirements. It permits the Channel Partner to order a Product to the Operator when it is mandated in the Order Delivery process of the Channel Partner. This happens when ApplicationOwner orders an API to Channel Partner.

A Service API is modeled as a Product (ProductOffering/ProductSpecification instance).

The order can be for subscribing or unsubscribing a Service API.

It also covers the retrieval to the Operator of the Channel Partner Products that result from these orders.

ChannelPartner Marketplace ApplicationOwner Management

ApplicationOwner cspAdmin

In the first part, the ApplicationOwner (Application Service Provider) registers with the Channel Partner. As a consequence, the Channel Partner presents the list of available Service APIs to the ApplicationOwner. Those APIs can be provided by different Operators, since the Channel Partner can have previous business agreements with several Operator.

# The ApplicationOwner then can select the list of APIs that fit its needs. It follows a sequence where the Channel Partner sends the Terms and Conditions for the ApplicationOwner to

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

accept. This sequence can be a loop where the ApplicationOwner registers on several Operators and accepts the Terms and Conditions of each of them.

Once the ApplicationOwner is registered and the Terms & Conditions have been accepted, the Channel Partner starts working directly with the Operator. For each Operator selected by the ApplicationOwner, the Channel Partner proceeds to onboard the ApplicationOwner in the Operator and then to onboard each of the Applications that the ApplicationOwner wants to register for the use of the Operator APIs.

In a third sequence, for each Application, one or more APIs are ordered to the Operator, who does internal work to create the new Products instances, together wih permissions and Terms & Conditions checking. When this internal processing is finished, the Operator informs the Channel Partner of the positive result of the request, that is, the activation of the APIs for the ApplicationOwner to use in its Application.

The Operate APIs to be used in this scenario are the following:

| Step | Description | Operation used |
| ---: | --- | --- |
| 8 | Onboarding ApplicationOwner | POST /applicationOwner |
| 11 | Onboard Application | POST /application |
| 16,17,19 | Application Approval StatusChange Event | POST /client/listener |
| 20 | Order API | POST/APIProductOrder |

The assumption is that manual checks can be taken on application level, and for initial ApplicationOwner creation both the ApplicationOwner itself as well as the first application can be assessed at the same time.

These operations may require a manual authorization, so has to be designed to be compatible with synchronous or asynchronous functional response.

This use case is preceded by the configuration of its products by the Operator and the initialization of the Channel Partner - Operator agreement. The information below is expected to be exchanged prior this use-case:

- Channel Partner ID
- Identifiers for the main agreed exposed Product Offering (Channel Partner Product Offering IDs) - optional
- Channel Partner Agreement Identification (Master Agreement)
- APIs to be ordered and enumeration for their scopes and purposes (Product Offering IDs, Product Offering Characteristics enumeration)
- Endpoint information for each API
- Terms and Conditiones per API/purpose/scopes
- Endpoint information for Operate APIs
- Channel Partner client id and client secret (for operate API calls)

## UC2: Application Creation for an existing ApplicationOwner

This use case covers onboarding a new Application for an ApplicationOwner which was already registered in the Channel Partner (and hence in the Operator) and providing access to Service APIs.

The use case is preceded by the Operator configuration of their products initialization of the Channel Partner Operator agreement, and creation of the ApplicationOwner.

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

The scenario starts in a similar way to Use Case 1. Now the process of ApplicationOwner onboarding is not needed, since the ApplicationOwner is already registered in the Channel Partner and the Operator. A new Application is registered on the Channel Partner, who then proceed to onboard the Application on the Operator. The onboarding includes the registration of the list of Service APIs needed for the Application, together to the internal Operator steps to create new Product and validate permissions and Terms & Conditions.

This function may require a manual authorization, so has to be designed to be compatible with synchronous or asynchronous functional response.

The use case allows for 2 variations of managing application digital identity: Digital Identity is created during application creation : Operate API will orchestrate the Operator security server returning back the client ID and client secret (Digital Identity is returned in application creation response) Digital identity not created during application creation : Seperate call need to be orchestrated by the Channel Partner directly to the Operator security server (Digital Identity not returned in application creation response)

The Operate APIs to be used in this scenario are the following:

| Step | Description | Operation used |
| ---: | --- | --- |
| 7 | Onboard Application | POST /application |
| 12/13/15 | Application Approval StateChange Event | POST/client/listener/applicationApprovalStatusChangeEvent |
| 16 | Order API | POST /apiProductOrder |

## UC3: API Access Ordering for an Existing Application

In this use case an Application get access to Service APIs. This use case is preceded by the Operator configuration of their products, the initialization of the Channel Partner Operator agreement, the creation of the ApplicationOwner as well granting application access to the API.

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

The ApplicationOwner selects one or several APIs/Scopes/Purposes already offered by the Channel Partner. The APIs could be provided by one or several Operators. For each of the Operators involved, the ApplicationOwner has to accept the Terms & Conditions. Once this is accomplished, the Channel Partner request onboarding for the APIs to the corresponding Operator. Each of the Operators does the internal work required to validate permissions and do Terms and Conditions checking. Activation of each of the APIs is notified to the Channel Partner.

The Operate APIs to be used in this scenario are the following:

| Step | Description | Operation used |
| ---: | --- | --- |
| 7 | Order API | POST/ apiProductOrder |

Operator providing the APIs and Applications that were using them should be specified. The Channel Partner in turn sends a removal request to the Operator. If there are more than one Operator or more than one API, the Channel Partner sends the removal requests in a loop until all removals have been sent. Each Operator confirms removal for all their APIs.

This operation implies that the ApplicationOwner, the Applications and the APIs have been previously registered on the Channel Partner and the Operator.

The Operate APIs to be used in this scenario are the following:

| Step | Description | Operation used |

## UC13: API Access Product Modification Ordering

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/jpeg;base64,)

In this use case, the ApplicationOwner wants to modify some of the API/Products which is already using. The change could affect the purpose for the API, or any other configurable characteristic of the ProductSpecification. After receiving the request from the ApplicationOwner, the Channel Partner detects the affected Products and present the ApplicationOwner the Terms and Conditions that must be accepted in order to be able to use the modified Products.

Then, the Channel Partner proceeds to request the modifications to each of the affected Operators. Each Operator has to validate permissions and terms and conditions. Once validations are done, the Operator sends a notification to the Channel Partner and the modification is finished.

The Operate APIs to be used in this scenario are the following:

| Step | Description | Operation used |
| ---: | --- | --- |
| 6 | Order API product for a change | POST /apiProductOrder |

# Support of polymorphism and extension patterns

Support of polymorphic collections and types and schema based extension is provided by means of a list of generic meta-attributes that we describe below. Polymorphism in collections occurs when entities inherit from base entities, for instance a BillingAccount and SettlementAccount inheriting properties from the abstract Account entity.

Generic support of polymorphism and pattern extensions is described in the TMF API Guidelines, Part 2 (TMF630).

The @type attribute provides a way to represent the actual class type of an entity. For example, within a list of Account instances some may be instances of BillingAccount where other could be instances of SettlementAccount. The @type gives this information. All resources and sub-resources of this API have a @type attributes that can be provided when this is useful.

The @referredType can be used within reference entities (like for instance an AccountRef object) to explicitly denote the actual entity type of the referred class. Notice that in reference entities the @type, when used, denotes the class type of the reference itself, such as BillingAccountRef or SettlementAccountRef, and not the class type of the referred object. However since reference classes are rarely sub-classed, @type is generally not useful in reference objects.

The @schemaLocation property can be used in resources to allow specifying user-defined properties of an Entity or to specify the expected characteristics of an entity.

The @baseType attribute gives a way to provide explicitly the base of class of a given resource that has been extended.

| externalIdentifier | An ExternalIdentifier. An identification of an entity that is ownedby or originates in a software system different from the currentsystem, for example a ProductOrder handed off from acommerce platform into an order handling system. The structureidentifies the system itself, the nature of the entity within thesystem (e.g. class name) and the unique ID of the entity withinthe system. It is anticipated that multiple external IDs can be heldfor a single entity, e.g. if the entity passed through multiplesystems on the way to the current system. In this case theconsumer is expected to sequence the IDs in the array in reverseorder of provenance, i.e. most recent system first in the list. |

### ApiProduct resource

### ApplicationOwner resource

Application Owner represents the role played by the organization that owns an Application that can consume API products. It's a specialization of a PartyRole in the Open Gateway context.

**ApplicationOwner fields**

| approvalStatus | An ApprovalStatusType. Valid values for an ApprovalStatus inthe context of an approval process. ENUMERATED with values:\* pendingApproval\* approved\* rejected |
| --- | --- |
| approvalStatusReason | A String. The reason why the approval status changed. |
| channelPartner | A PartyRoleRef. Party role reference. A party role represents thepart played by a party in a given context. |
| creationDate | A DateTime. Date and time when the ApplicationOwner wascreated. |
| description | A String. A description of the ApplicationOwner. |
| engagedParty | An ApplicationOwnerOrganization. Application Organizationrepresents a group of people identified by shared interests orpurpose. Examples include business, department and enterprise.Because of the complex nature of many businesses, bothorganizations and organization units are represented by thesame data. It’s a specialization of Party in the Open Gatewaycontext. |

This notification structure owns an event payload structure ("SpecificEventPayload" placeholder) linked to the resource concerned by the notification using the resource name as access field ("resourceName" placeholder).

# API OPERATIONS 

Note: Many of the resource and payload examples include sample values for Attachment.content. These sample values are not syntactically correct, since any realistic value for content would be far too large and would obscure the readability of the examples.

Remember the following Uniform Contract:

| Operation on Entities | Uniform API Operation | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Query Entities | GET Resource | GET must be used to retrieve arepresentation of a resource. |
| Create Entity | POST Resource | POST must be used to create anew resource |
| Partial Update of an Entity | PATCH Resource | PATCH must be used to partiallyupdate a resource |
| Remove an Entity | DELETE Resource | DELETE must be used toremove a resource |
| Execute an Action on an Entity | POST on TASK Resource | POST must be used to executeTask Resources |
| Other Request Methods | POST on TASK Resource | GET and POST must not beused to tunnel other requestmethods. |

Filtering and attribute selection rules are described in the TMF REST Design Guidelines.

Monitor pattern, as described in TMF630 REST Design Guidelines, SHALL be used when supporting Async requests. A Monitor resource is created for each async operation. For example, in a resource creation operation HTTP POST, the returned 202 Accept response shall have a Link header referencing the monitor created to check the operation status. The consumer can check regularly using the Link in order to check the status of the operation.

```
Link: <https://mycsp.com/tmf-api/productOrderingManagement/v5/monitor/77795e7f-5213-4b9c-b672-6838a6b76152>;rel=related;title=monitor,
```

(where the 77795e7f-5213-4b9c-b672-6838a6b76152 is the monitor resource identifier assigned for this resource)

Notifications are also described in a subsequent section.

### Updates partially a Application

```
PATCH /application/{id}?fields=…
```

**Description**

This operation allows partial updates of an Application entity. Support of json/merge ([https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7396)](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7396) is mandatory, support of json/patch ([http://tools.ietf.org/](http://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc5789) [html/rfc5789)](http://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc5789) is optional. Note: If the update operation yields to the creation of sub-resources or relationships, the same rules concerning mandatory sub-resource attributes and default value settings in the POST operation applies to the PATCH operation. Hence these tables are not repeated here.

**Patchable and Non Patchable Attributes**

| **Non Patchable Attributes** | **Rule** |
| --- | --- |
| apiConsumerRole |  |
| applicationOwner |  |
| approvalStatus |  |
| channelPartner |  |
| creationDate |  |
| @baseType | @baseType is immutable |
| @schemaLocation | @schemaLocation is immutable |
| @type | @type is immutable |

### Updates partially a ApplicationOwner

```
PATCH /applicationOwner/{id}?fields=…
```

**Description**

This operation allows partial updates of an ApplicationOwner entity. Support of json/merge ([https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7396)](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7396) is mandatory, support of json/patch ([http://tools.ietf.org/](http://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc5789) [html/rfc5789)](http://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc5789) is optional. Note: If the update operation yields to the creation of sub-resources or relationships, the same rules concerning mandatory sub-resource attributes and default value settings in the POST operation applies to the PATCH operation. Hence these tables are not repeated here.

**Patchable and Non Patchable Attributes**

| --- | --- |
| approvalStatus |  |
| approvalStatusReason |  |
| channelPartner |  |
| creationDate |  |
| href |  |
| id |  |
| validFor |  |

| --- | --- |
| @baseType | @baseType is immutable |
| @schemaLocation | @schemaLocation is immutable |
| @type | @type is immutable |

| **Patchable Attributes** | **Rule** |
| --- | --- |
| description |  |
| engagedParty |  |
| name |  |
| status |  |
| statusReason |  |

# API NOTIFICATIONS 

For every single of operation on the entities use the following templates and provide sample REST notification POST calls.

It is assumed that the Pub/Sub uses the Register and UnRegister mechanisms described in the REST Guidelines reproduced below.

## Register listener

**POST /hub**

**Description**

Sets the communication endpoint address the service instance must use to deliver information about its health state, execution state, failures and metrics. Subsequent POST calls will be rejected by the service if it does not support multiple listeners. In this case DELETE /api/hub/{id} must be called before an endpoint can be created again.

**Behavior**

Returns HTTP/1.1 status code 201 if the request was successful.

**Usage Samples**

Here’s an example of a request for registering a listener.

**Request**

```
POST /api/hub
Accept: application/json
{
    "callback": "http://in.listener.com"
}
```

**Response**

```
Content-Type: application/json
Location: /api/hub/42
{
    "id":"42",
    "callback": "http://in.listener.com",    "query":""
}
```

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

## Unregister listener

**DELETE /hub/{id}**

**Description**

Clears the communication endpoint address that was set by creating the Hub..

**Behavior**

Returns HTTP/1.1 status code 204 if the request was successful.

Returns HTTP/1.1 status code 404 if the resource is not found.

**Usage Samples**

Here’s an example of a request for un-registering a listener.

**Request**

```
DELETE /api/hub/42
Accept: application/json
```

**Response**

```
204
```

## Publish Event to listener

**POST /client/listener**

**Description**

Clears the communication endpoint address that was set by creating the Hub.

Provides to a registered listener the description of the event that was raised. The /client/listener url is the callback url passed when registering the listener.

**Behavior**

Returns HTTP/1.1 status code 201 if the service is able to set the configuration.

**Usage Samples**

Here’s an example of a notification received by the listener. In this example “EVENT TYPE” should be replaced by one of the notification types supported by this API (see Notification resources Models section) and EVENT BODY refers to the data structure of the given notification type.

**Request**

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

```
POST /client/listener
Accept: application/json
{
    "event": {
        EVENT BODY    },
    "eventType": "EVENT_TYPE"
}
```

**Response**

```
201
```

For detailed examples on the general TM Forum notification mechanism, see the TMF REST Design Guidelines.

## Release description v5.2.1 (vs 5.2.0)

### Conformance Profile

additional comment on the optional attribute approvedProductOfferingTermOrCondition.applicationLegalBasisForInputData

## Release description v5.2.0 (vs 5.1.2)

### Operations

additional parameters added by tooling generation (before, after, sort, filter)

### Schemas

Changed schemas and add new schemas to allow ordering of composite ProductOffering (bundles)

Changed ApiProduct schema to allow inventory of composite products (bundles) : added productRelationship to ApiProduct

Added example schemas ApiProductLocationVerificationAntifraud and UsageVolumeProductLocationVerification

Replacement of many \[entity\]\_FVO schemas with \[entity\] schemas , that has impact on many attributes being optional in the POST operation (optional in the OAS but not in the

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

conformance profile, so must be kept mandatory in the implementations)

Added stateReason in ApiProductOrder and all ApiProductOrderItem specialized schemas

Added externalIdentifier in ApiProductOrderItemAdd schema

Added creationDate in ApplicationOwner and Application

Added descriptions

### User Guide

Additional description of entities for consistency with TMF936 Product Catalog Operate API

Added description of Monitor

### Examples

Examples updated for better consistency with GSMA requirements and TMF936 Product Catalog Operate API (based on same catalog examples, allowing bundles ordering and inventory)

Examples updated for better general precision (dates, ids, …)

## Release description v5.1.0 (vs 5.0.0)

### End-point changes

**Hub**

Adding GET /hub/{id}

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

### Type changes

**ApiDigitalIdentity**

Marked as deprecated (as input and patchable property)

Marked as deprecated fields:

- clientId (as input property)
- redirectUrl (moved to Application type)
- jwksUri(moved to Application type)

**ApiPermissionSet**

Marked as deprecated fields:

- validFor

**ApiProduct**

Added properties to be aligned with future TMF936 Open Gateway Catalogue API:

- purpose
- countryCode (array of ISO country codes of 2 letters: pattern '\[A-Z\]{2}')

**Application**

New properties:

- redirectUrl (moved from ApiDigitalIdentity type)
- jwksUri (moved from ApiDigitalIdentity type)

New GDPR required property :

- privacyRightsRequestContact (of ContactMedium type)

Marked as deprecated fields :

- approvalStatusReason (as patchable property)

**ApplicationOwnerOrganization**

New Properties:

- localRepresentative of type AplicationOwnerRelatedLocalRepresentative

**ApplicationOwnerRelatedOrganization**

Changed properties from string to enum:

- organizationType

![](data:image/png;base64,)

![](data:image/png;base64,)

Updated property:

- organizationType enum from list of [https://www.w3.org/community/reports/dpvcg/CG-](https://www.w3.org/community/reports/dpvcg/CG-FINAL-dpv-20221205/#vocab-entities-organisation) [FINAL-dpv-20221205/#vocab-entities-organisation](https://www.w3.org/community/reports/dpvcg/CG-FINAL-dpv-20221205/#vocab-entities-organisation)

**DataExportCountry**

New type for GDPR required properties with :

- countryCode (ISO country codes of 2 letters: pattern '\[A-Z\]{2}')
- commercialActivity (boolean)
- commercialOrganizationName (string)
- dataPrivacyFrameworkURL (url) only for EU-USA data privacy agreement.

**ProductOfferingTermOrCondition**

New property:

- product reference to ApiProduct (optional)

New GDPR properties (optional):

- applicationLegalBasisForInputData (enum from DpvLegalBasisType)
- dataExportTransitCountry (array of DataExportCountry)
- dataExportStorageCountry (array of DataExportCountry)
- duration (enum from DpvDurationType)
- frequency (enum from DpvFrequencyType)
- processingContext (enum from DpvContextClassesType)
- processingOperation (enum from DpvProcessingOperationType)
- purposeReason (string)
- userConsentScreenshot (file attached, described in SimpleAttachment schema)

**ProductOfferingTermOrConditionApproval**

Marked as deprecated:

- authorization (it is not possible to get the id of the individual authorizing the order)

**RelatedOrderItem**

Marked as deprecated:

- role

**WebFormContactMedium**

New ContactMedium sub-type with property url.

![](data:image/png;base64,)

Bug fixed on discriminator list of GCProductOrderItem and GCProductOrderItem\_FVO schemas

Some examples bug fixed (ApiProductOrder, ApplicationOwner, Application)

Some examples added according to new attributes in OAS.

### User Guide changes

New diagram for Use Case 1

Some minor fixes (wording, dates)

Extension of strongly typed schemas chapter with examples and schemas

### Conformance Profile changes

Added possibility of asynchronous responses with code 202 in addition of synchronous with code 201; in that case Monitor ressource is mandatory in GET operation

Added specific rules on specific legislations (GDPR for Europe, Canada, USA)

New attributes added (based on changes in the OAS)

Some minor fixes (wording, dates)
